title: Sebastian election results: who won the two council seats, and which charter questions passed
seoTitle: Sebastian Election Results 2026: Council and Charter
description: Sherrie Matthews and Deborah Shellenberger won Sebastian council seats. Two of three charter questions passed; the council pay raise did not.
dek: Sebastian voters filled two City Council seats on Tuesday and decided three changes to the city charter. Here are the unofficial numbers, what each question does, and what the new council faces first.
facebook: Sebastian voted Tuesday. Who got the two council seats, and did the council pay raise pass? Here are the numbers in plain English, what the three charter questions change, and the big decisions waiting for the new council.

body.text: The votes are counted in Sebastian. On Tuesday, voters inside city limits filled two of the five City Council seats and answered three questions that change the city charter, the city's basic rulebook.
These are the final but unofficial results reported by TCPalm. They become official once the county certifies them. This article sticks to the facts: who won, what passed, and what happens next.

body.title: The short version
body.text: Sherrie Matthews was reelected and Deborah Shellenberger won the seat Ed Dodd is leaving. Voters approved a longer residency rule for council candidates and the question about the governor's power to suspend and remove council members. They turned down a council pay raise.
Who won the two council seats
Five candidates ran for two at-large seats. At-large means the whole city votes on every seat. Here are the unofficial results:

Shellenberger replaces Ed Dodd, who did not seek a sixth term. Each seat carries a two-year term. Sebastian does not elect its mayor directly. Under the city charter, the council chooses its mayor and vice mayor from among its own members.
Voters approved two of the three questions and rejected one. Here is how TCPalm summarized each one, with the unofficial results.

items: Question 1, residency for candidates: PASSED, 90.3% yes (11,383) to 9.7% no (1,219). Council candidates must now live in city limits for two years instead of one, with continuous residency and a physical presence in the city at least 270 days a year.

Question 2, council pay: FAILED, 42.7% yes (5,342) to 57.3% no (7,172). It would have raised monthly pay from $450 to $750 for the mayor and from $300 to $600 for the vice mayor and other members, with yearly raises matching the cost-of-living raises other city workers get.

Question 3, the governor and council members: PASSED, 84.8% yes (10,608) to 15.2% no (1,895). TCPalm described it as dealing with the governor's power to suspend, remove and reinstate council members, and to revoke suspensions.

body.text: Because the pay question failed, council pay stays at $450 a month for the mayor and $300 a month for the vice mayor and other members.

Sebastian voters have said no to council pay raises before. TCPalm reported that 71% opposed a raise in 2016 and 59% rejected a similar question in 2007. In 2024, 58% voted against stretching council terms from two years to four.
The decisions coming up land right on Sebastian homes. TCPalm listed the big ones:

items: The Graves Brothers land. The city annexed 2,044 acres of former citrus land in 2023. It is the largest undeveloped area in Sebastian, and the next council will shape what gets built there.
More growth. This year the council approved annexing 586 acres for 1,758 homes.

Water and sewer. Indian River County provides water and sewer in Sebastian. The city has to work with the county to make sure there is enough capacity for new homes, and to move an estimated 11,000 septic-tank parcels onto sewer.
Keeping the feel of the town. Every candidate said they want to protect Sebastian's small-town, fishing-village character.

body.text: There is one more result that touches every homesteaded Sebastian house. Statewide Amendment 3 passed with 62% of the vote, CBS12 reported. It raises the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and to $250,000 in 2028. The city's own tax line is a non-school tax, so the council will be planning budgets with that change in mind.

items: Check the final count. Tuesday's numbers are unofficial until certified. The Indian River County Supervisor of Elections posts results at voteindianriver.gov.
Watch for the council's organizational meeting. That is where the new council picks its mayor and vice mayor. Agendas are posted in the Agenda Center at cityofsebastian.org.
Follow the Graves land and annexation hearings. If you live near the edges of the city, these votes decide what goes up next to you. Meeting agendas list each hearing ahead of time.
On septic? Keep an eye on the county's sewer plans for your street. The city and county have to work together on the conversions.
Want to reach your council? The City Clerk's office at City Hall, 1225 Main Street, can tell you how to contact members or speak at a meeting.

body.text: Two new terms start, three charter questions are settled, and the big growth decisions are still ahead. Showing up at a meeting is the next step if you want a say.

faq.q: Who won the Sebastian City Council election in 2026?
faq.a: Unofficial results show incumbent Sherrie Matthews (31.90%) and Deborah Shellenberger (21.50%) won the two open seats. Each term is two years.

faq.q: Did the Sebastian council pay raise pass?
faq.a: No. Question 2 failed with 57.3% voting no. Pay stays at $450 a month for the mayor and $300 a month for the vice mayor and other council members.

faq.q: What charter questions passed in Sebastian?
faq.a: Question 1, which requires council candidates to live in the city for two years with a physical presence at least 270 days a year, and Question 3, about the governor's power to suspend, remove and reinstate council members.

faq.q: How is the mayor of Sebastian chosen?
faq.a: Sebastian voters do not elect the mayor directly. The five council members choose the mayor and vice mayor from among themselves.
